Mangroves restored. Habitats improved. But fish catches still declining by 6.52 kg per trip. SPIBES student Irene Mbuthye Mwendwa’s brief on coastal restoration in Watamu, Kenya, shows why ecology and livelihoods must be tackled together. 👇

The Arabuko-Sokoke Forest is Kenya's largest intact coastal dry forest, a biodiversity hotspot near Watamu, vital for endemic species like the golden-rumped elephant shrew and Clarke's weaver, featuring diverse habitats and offering eco-tourism like birdwatching and walking trails
